purpose: Test whether the 0xFFDD00 object-record writer stream depends on wall-clock timing when replaying the same recorded race.

course_write_sidecar.interpretation: The object-window transition burst at frame 883 follows input/transition-state writes to 0xFF957A/0xFF957C; no course-index write to 0xFF9578 occurs in this interval.

verdict: WALL-CLOCK-INVARIANT; FRAME-LOCKED VS POSITION-LOCKED NOT DISCRIMINATED
interpretation: A deliberate two-second wall-clock pause at emulated frame 900 leaves the complete recorded input and 0xFFDD00 write event stream unchanged. The run is deterministic and not wall-clock-triggered. Because the replay trajectory and emulated frame counter are identical in all runs, this experiment cannot distinguish an emulated-frame trigger from a track-position trigger. The sidecar also shows that the frame-883 object burst is not accompanied by a course-index write to 0xFF9578; it follows writes to the adjacent input/transition-state fields 0xFF957A/0xFF957C.
